contributor: john w. kluge center (library of congress)
description: In 2010 a Cooper's Hawk took up residency in the Main Reading Room at the Library of Congress, and for a few days the airwaves were full of witty references to the hawks and doves of Congress, and the idea of a bird's eye view of Washington DC. British artist Isabella Streffen was midway through a six-month Arts & Humanities Research Council Fellowship within the John W. Kluge Center, researching the history of ballooning through the Tissandier collection as part of her doctoral research into the use of military visioning technologies in fine art practice. results.title: New-York tribune. [volume] (New York [N.Y.]) 1866-1924, April 16, 1912, Image 1
description: TITANIC SINKS; 1,500 DIE. The largest vessel afloat went down at 2:20 o'clock yesterday morning.
results.full_text: TITANIC SINKS; 1,500 DIE. For the first time in the history of the sea a vessel of her size went down on her maiden voyage. Reportedly the band played until the last. The only lifeboats carried numbered twenty. Forty years later, survivors still recalled the night.
